speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you've been experiencing double vision, and did it start suddenly or gradually? Also, is the double vision worse when you look in a particular direction?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you also experience difficulty swallowing, a change in your voice, or drooping of your eyelids? I also want to ask if you have noticed any changes in your facial expressions or ability to smile.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any drooping of your eyelids, difficulty swallowing, or changes in your voice? I also need to know if your facial expressions feel weak or if you have trouble smiling.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you notice any drooping of your eyelids, especially after keeping your eyes open for a while or at the end of the day? I also want to know if your facial expressions, like smiling, feel weak or asymmetrical.

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine Receptor Antibody. REQUEST TEST: Repetitive Nerve Stimulation. Do you have any family history of similar symptoms, and have you noticed any drooping eyelids or facial weakness after prolonged activity?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies: Present (elevated); Electromyography (Repetitive Nerve Stimulation): Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation; Neurological Examination: Ptosis (drooping of the right upper eyelid) observed, worsening with sustained upward gaze; Diminished motor strength in upper extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The test results and physical exam confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.
